title: command
description:
Client -> daemon priority/latched command. estop hard-latches; reset_latch clears e_stop_latched and must be reachable even while in safe-stop.

TWO SHAPES, both accepted. The `name` form is this schema's original dialect. The FLAG form ({"estop": true}) is what every deployed client actually sends -- the bridge forwards it verbatim and the L2 broker matches it -- so the schema admits it rather than describing a dialect nothing speaks.

DANGER, L2 -- THE VALUE IS NOT READ. The broker decides by SUBSTRING on the raw line, so any command frame merely CONTAINING the text triggers the action regardless of its value:
  {"estop": false}        trips the e-stop  (annoying, but fail-safe)
  {"reset_latch": false}  CLEARS AN E-STOP  (fail-DANGEROUS)
The second is the one that matters: a client that helpfully sends every field with an explicit false, or that includes the word in a note field, silently un-latches a stopped robot. Both flags are therefore pinned to `const: true` here -- send the key or omit it, never send it false.

AUTHENTICATION: there is NONE at this layer. This schema previously required a `token` alongside `reset_latch`, which read as an auth control but was never enforced -- the daemon parses `token` only out of `hello`, and the broker reads no token here at all. The requirement has been dropped so the schema describes reality, and the absence is recorded here rather than left implied: ANY client already admitted to the session can clear an E-STOP. The only gate is upstream -- Supabase RLS on the signaling room decides who may connect at all.

token.description: Legacy field. Not sent by any current client and not read by the daemon, which takes its agent token from `hello` at connect. Retained so an older client's frame still validates.
